question: Is the opposite MACS0429 response sign associated with a directly observed star-gas morphology distinction?
interpretation: post-hoc four-system descriptor audit that may nominate, but cannot validate, an environmental gate

maps.stars: registered nonnegative CLASH F160W light after lens-image masking
maps.gas: registered point-source-masked Chandra 0.7-2.0 keV map, Gaussian smoothed at 3 arcsec and square-root transformed
maps.normalization: normalize each component independently inside every aperture

ranking.score: signed difference from positive-group mean divided by positive-group sample standard deviation with a 1e-6 floor
ranking.claim_rule: rank candidates descriptively; no threshold, p-value, formula selection, or promotion

claim_limits: One negative-sign cluster and three positive-sign clusters cannot establish a population relationship.
The response labels were known before this descriptor audit, so every ranking is post-hoc.
X-ray brightness remains an angular morphology proxy rather than a local gas-mass measurement.
Any nominated gate must be frozen and tested on new clusters before entering a gravity formula.
No formula can be promoted from P0564.
